grades.quote: RISC-V base ISAs have either little-endian or big-endian memory systems, with the privileged architecture further defining bi-endian operation. Instructions are stored in memory as a sequence of 16-bit little-endian parcels, regardless of memory system endianness.
grades.reason: Directly answers the RISC-V side, distinguishing memory-system endianness from fixed instruction byte order.
Discusses ordering and coherence of memory operations, not memory byte order.
Describes cache-block zeroing and update granularity, not endianness.
Defines data widths and two’s-complement encoding but gives no memory byte-order rules.
